Ui.Script:
-- The static category tree (era Game tab, Classic tocs), in list order. Keys are the row -- name suffixes; the visible label doubles as the page title (the era does the same — -- Settings.RegisterCategory names both from one string). OPTIONS_CATEGORY_KEYS = { "Controls", "Interface", "ActionBars", "Combat", "Social", "Keybindings", "Nameplates", "Graphics", "Audio", }
-- The era-window scale (shared, director-owned — the 0219 WORLDMAP_WINDOWED_SCALE -- pattern): the era client's UIParent draws smaller against the screen than our 1.12 -- 768-canvas does on modern displays, and this knob is that mapping — every era-shaped -- window wears it (this window here; GameMenuFrame in its OnShow — in the era both draw -- at the SAME UIParent px-per-unit, the parity the director's eye checked). At 1.0 the -- 724-tall window fills ~85% of the screen's height in our 768-virtual space, where the -- reference at typical resolutions reads nearer two-thirds. ERA_WINDOW_SCALE = 0.78
function OptionsFrame_UpdateScale() -- The era panel is registered `checkFit = 1`: the panel manager also shrinks it to -- fit a small screen (UIPanelUpdateScaleForFit: min over width/height ratios -- against the panel + 20 units of air each way, capped at 1) — transcribed here. local k = ERA_WINDOW_SCALE local wFit = GetScreenWidth() / 940 local hFit = GetScreenHeight() / 744 if wFit < k then k = wFit end if hFit < k then k = hFit end OptionsFrame:SetScale(k) end
-- The era tab width law (MinimalTab.lua l.7): label width + 40. Era measures at OnLoad; -- our measure round-trip answers a frame late, so OnUpdate polls until the width is real -- (the chat-header converge idiom), then latches. Deliberate divergence: the era -- measures with the MEDIUM font it is about to swap away (an accident of its code -- order, ~6 units of extra padding); we measure the small font the label actually -- wears. function OptionsTab_FitWidth(tab) if tab.fitted then return end local w = getglobal(tab:GetName() .. "Text"):GetStringWidth() if w and w > 0 then tab:SetWidth(w + 40) tab.fitted = true end end
-- Each row's OnLoad: remember the key + title, paint the label, size the wash plate — -- the era sized it via SetAtlas(name, true) at atlas size (187x21, centered: 6 units -- in from either edge of the 199 row); with plain SetTexture the size is authored -- here once — and set the 1.14 base tint: OptionsListButton_OnLoad's own -- SetVertexColor(.196, .388, .8), the steel-blue every unselected row's hover wears -- (OptionsFrameTemplates.lua l.130-131). The whole row identity lives here so adding -- a category is one XML row + one key in the table above. function OptionsCategoryRow_OnLoad(row, key, label) row.categoryKey = key row.pageTitle = label row:SetText(label) local bg = getglobal(row:GetName() .. "Bg") bg:SetWidth(187) bg:SetHeight(21) bg:SetVertexColor(0.196, 0.388, 0.8) end
-- The selection — 1.14's OptionsList_SelectButton/_ClearSelection pair, verbatim -- (OptionsFrameTemplates.lua l.107-121): the selected row's wash goes GOLD (1,1,0) -- and locks on; every other row drops back to the blue hover tint, wash off. The -- white selected label is LockHighlight's own text state, carried by the font swap. -- Also the era law on top (SettingsPanelMixin:SelectCategory clears the search box — -- Blizzard_SettingsPanel.lua l.793): picking a category ENDS a live search; the -- SetText("") round-trips through OnTextChanged -> restore -> back here, so this call -- returns early and lets the re-entry do the work once. -- Then the page swap: a category with rows (OPTIONS_PAGE_ROWS) shows its body -- refreshed from the CVars and Defaults goes live with it; every other page is still -- empty, Defaults disabled. function OptionsFrame_SelectCategory(key) OptionsFrame.selectedCategory = key if OptionsFrameSearchBox:GetText() ~= "" then OptionsFrameSearchBox:SetText("") return -- the OnTextChanged restore re-entered with this same key and finished end for _, k in ipairs(OPTIONS_CATEGORY_KEYS) do local row = getglobal("OptionsFrameCategoryListRow" .. k) local bg = getglobal("OptionsFrameCategoryListRow" .. k .. "Bg") if k == key then bg:SetVertexColor(1, 1, 0) bg:Show() row:SetTextFontObject("GameFontHighlight") OptionsFrameContainerTitle:SetText(row.pageTitle) else bg:SetVertexColor(0.196, 0.388, 0.8) bg:Hide() row:SetTextFontObject("GameFontNormal") end end for k in pairs(OPTIONS_PAGE_ROWS) do local body = getglobal("OptionsFrameContainerBody" .. k) if k == key then body:Show() else body:Hide() end end -- The Keybindings page (KeyBindingsPage.xml, decision 1008) body-swaps like the -- CVar pages but runs its own machinery: entering rebuilds the section tree; -- leaving disarms a straggling capture (the host seam must never outlive the page) -- and clears its message line. Its Defaults is the confirmed Reset To Default (the -- button's OnClick forks), and the Unbind Key button exists only here. local kb = getglobal("OptionsFrameContainerBodyKeybindings") if key == "Keybindings" then kb:Show() KeyBindingsPage_Refresh() OptionsFrameContainerUnbind:Show() OptionsFrameContainerDefaults:Enable() else kb:Hide() KeyBindings_SetSelected(nil) KeyBindings_Output("") OptionsFrameContainerUnbind:Hide() if OPTIONS_PAGE_ROWS[key] then OptionsPage_Refresh(key) OptionsFrameContainerDefaults:Enable() else OptionsFrameContainerDefaults:Disable() end end end
-- ── Search (0984): the era SettingsPanel mechanism, transcribed ───────────────────── -- Blizzard_SettingsPanel.lua l.566-692 + Blizzard_Settings.lua l.65-77, cut to our -- static rows: a setting's search tag is its LABEL uppercased (the era's default tag -- is exactly the setting name — SettingControls.lua l.773); a query matches by plain -- substring, scored by matched-word length; matches group under their category, the -- groups ordered by their best score; each group opens with a clickable category -- header (SettingsListSearchCategoryTemplate — click = jump to the category, which -- ends the search); no match shows the section-header "no results" line. The results -- ARE the live rows — the era reflows the real initializers into a fresh vertical -- layout, so ours re-anchor the real row frames (values, writes, dependencies all -- work in place) and the restore path lays every page back down by the one layout -- law below.
-- The era's word list (l.569-572): the WHOLE query first — a phrase match outranks -- its own words — then every comma/space-separated token. function OptionsSearch_Words(text) local up = string.upper(text) local words = { up } for w in string.gfind(up, "([^, ]+)") do table.insert(words, w) end return words end
-- The era score (Blizzard_Settings.lua l.65-77 MatchesSearchTags): first word that -- hits the tag scores last-first (matched length - 1); no hit is no match. Plain -- find — the era passes plain=true, no pattern magic. function OptionsSearch_Score(tag, words) for _, w in ipairs(words) do local first, last = string.find(tag, w, 1, true) if first then return last - first end end return nil end
-- The era gather+group (l.575-636): rows bucketed by score, scores walked high to -- low; a category's group is born the first time one of its rows surfaces — so the -- group ORDER is best-score order — and collects that category's matches as the walk -- descends. Returns the ordered group list { key, rkeys } .. . function OptionsSearch_FindMatches(text) local words = OptionsSearch_Words(text) local buckets, scores = {}, {} for _, key in ipairs(OPTIONS_CATEGORY_KEYS) do if OPTIONS_PAGE_ROWS[key] then for _, rkey in ipairs(OPTIONS_PAGE_ROWS[key]) do local row = getglobal("OptionsFrameContainerBody" .. key .. rkey) local s = OptionsSearch_Score(row.searchTag, words) if s then if not buckets[s] then buckets[s] = {} table.insert(scores, s) end table.insert(buckets[s], { key = key, rkey = rkey }) end end end end -- The keybinding entries join the same buckets (the era's searchable fake category -- whose results REDIRECT to the Keybindings page — KeyBindingsPage.xml's search -- note). Their rkey is the BINDING INDEX; the display fork below tells them apart -- by the group key. for _, m in ipairs(KeyBindings_SearchMatches(words)) do if not buckets[m.score] then buckets[m.score] = {} table.insert(scores, m.score) end table.insert(buckets[m.score], { key = "Keybindings", rkey = m.index }) end table.sort(scores, function(a, b) return a > b end) local groups, order = {}, {} for _, s in ipairs(scores) do for _, m in ipairs(buckets[s]) do if not groups[m.key] then groups[m.key] = {} table.insert(order, m.key) end table.insert(groups[m.key], m.rkey) end end return order, groups end
-- ── The page scroll (B217) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- The body is the scroll child (the ScrollFrame above it), so what these two do is -- decide how TALL it is: the content's own extent, or the visible page rect, whichever -- is larger. Below the rect nothing changes at all — range 0, no bar, every page seated -- exactly where its XML puts it — and above it the overflow becomes a scroll instead of -- a spill. -- -- The measured set is every element that takes a seat in the ONE layout law's chain: -- each page's rows, the search group heads, and the keybinding result pool. All of them -- hang off the body's TOP, so their extent is independent of the height being computed — -- which is what makes this converge. Nothing anchored to the body's BOTTOM may join them -- (the Keybindings page's output line is the live example): growing the body would move -- it down, which would grow the body. IsVisible, not IsShown: a hidden page's rows keep -- their own shown flag, and only what the player can actually see may set the height. function OptionsScroll_ContentBottom() local bottom = nil local function take(name) local f = getglobal(name) if f and f:IsVisible() then local b = f:GetBottom() if b and (not bottom or b < bottom) then bottom = b end end end for _, key in ipairs(OPTIONS_CATEGORY_KEYS) do if OPTIONS_PAGE_ROWS[key] then take("OptionsFrameContainerBodySearchHead" .. key) for _, rkey in ipairs(OPTIONS_PAGE_ROWS[key]) do take("OptionsFrameContainerBody" .. key .. rkey) end end end take("OptionsFrameContainerBodySearchHeadKeybindings") for i = 1, KEYBINDINGS_SEARCH_ROWS do take("OptionsFrameContainerBodyKeybindSearch" .. i) end return bottom end
-- Size the body to that, from the scroll frame's OnUpdate. Frame-late by nature (rects -- resolve after Lua runs, so a reflow answers a frame later — the OptionsTab_FitWidth -- idiom), and write-gated: SetWidth/SetHeight invalidate layout, so an every-frame write -- would fight the resolver. UpdateScrollChildRect re-drives the bar through -- OnScrollRangeChanged, which is what shows and hides it (and its trough). function OptionsScroll_Fit() local sf = OptionsFrameContainerScroll local body = OptionsFrameContainerBody local fw, fh = sf:GetWidth(), sf:GetHeight() if not fw or fw <= 0 or not fh or fh <= 0 then return end if math.abs(body:GetWidth() - fw) >= 0.5 then body:SetWidth(fw) end local h = fh local top, bottom = body:GetTop(), OptionsScroll_ContentBottom() if top and bottom then local content = (top - bottom) + BENILLA_SCROLL_PAD if content > h then h = content end end if math.abs(body:GetHeight() - h) >= 0.5 then body:SetHeight(h) sf:UpdateScrollChildRect() end end
-- THE one layout law (era SettingsList: verticalPad 10, padLeft 25/padRight 0 → -- first element at (10,-12) off the body, spacing 9 → chain at (0,-9)). The rows' -- authored XML anchors state exactly this chain as the initial layout; search -- reflows steal rows out of it, and this function is how ANY element — row or search -- head — takes a seat in it. prev is a global frame NAME (nil = the chain head). function OptionsSearch_Place(name, prev) local f = getglobal(name) f:ClearAllPoints() if prev then f:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", prev, "BOTTOMLEFT", 0, -9) f:SetPoint("TOPRIGHT", prev, "BOTTOMRIGHT", 0, -9) else f:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", "OptionsFrameContainerBody", "TOPLEFT", 10, -12) f:SetPoint("TOPRIGHT", "OptionsFrameContainerBody", "TOPRIGHT", -20, -12) end end
-- Lay a page's rows back down on their authored chain (the XML anchors' law, -- re-stated after a search reflow; the pin test holds the two equal). function OptionsPage_Layout(key) local prev = nil for _, rkey in ipairs(OPTIONS_PAGE_ROWS[key]) do local name = "OptionsFrameContainerBody" .. key .. rkey OptionsSearch_Place(name, prev) getglobal(name):Show() prev = name end end
-- The results view (era OnSearchTextChanged's hasText arm, l.659-691): every page -- body SHOWS (they are bare row hosts sharing one rect) with every row hidden, then -- the groups chain down — category head, then its matches; a matched CHILD row pulls -- its parent row in first (l.665-670, the era parentInitializer rule — our Audio -- volumes ride under Master). Title reads "Search Results", Defaults hides while the -- search holds the page (l.684-688), and an empty result shows the no-results line -- (l.680-682). function OptionsSearch_Display(text) -- A new result set starts at the top (the era's own ScrollBox reset on a search). OptionsFrameContainerScroll:SetVerticalScroll(0) for k in pairs(OPTIONS_PAGE_ROWS) do getglobal("OptionsFrameContainerBody" .. k):Show() for _, rkey in ipairs(OPTIONS_PAGE_ROWS[k]) do getglobal("OptionsFrameContainerBody" .. k .. rkey):Hide() end getglobal("OptionsFrameContainerBodySearchHead" .. k):Hide() end -- The Keybindings furniture leaves the stage with the rest: its body hides (the -- search paints matched bindings on the shared pool below, not the page list), a -- straggling capture disarms, and the pool starts blank. getglobal("OptionsFrameContainerBodyKeybindings"):Hide() getglobal("OptionsFrameContainerBodySearchHeadKeybindings"):Hide() for i = 1, KEYBINDINGS_SEARCH_ROWS do getglobal("OptionsFrameContainerBodyKeybindSearch" .. i):Hide() end KeyBindingsPage.searchPainted = nil KeyBindings_SetSelected(nil) OptionsFrameContainerUnbind:Hide() OptionsFrameContainerTitle:SetText("Search Results") OptionsFrameContainerDefaults:Hide()
local order, groups = OptionsSearch_FindMatches(text) if table.getn(order) == 0 then OptionsFrameContainerBodyNoResults:Show() return end OptionsFrameContainerBodyNoResults:Hide() local prev = nil for _, key in ipairs(order) do local head = "OptionsFrameContainerBodySearchHead" .. key OptionsSearch_Place(head, prev) getglobal(head):Show() prev = head if key == "Keybindings" then -- Matched bindings painted LIVE onto the static pool (the era reflows its -- real rows the same way; the pool caps the count — the SCOPE note in -- KeyBindingsPage.xml — and the head above jumps to the full page). KeyBindingsPage.searchPainted = {} local shown = 0 for _, index in ipairs(groups[key]) do if shown < KEYBINDINGS_SEARCH_ROWS then shown = shown + 1 local name = "OptionsFrameContainerBodyKeybindSearch" .. shown KeyBindings_PaintBindRow(name, index) OptionsSearch_Place(name, prev) getglobal(name):Show() KeyBindingsPage.searchPainted[name] = index prev = name end end else local placed = {} for _, rkey in ipairs(groups[key]) do local row = getglobal("OptionsFrameContainerBody" .. key .. rkey) if row.parentRow and not placed[row.parentRow] then placed[row.parentRow] = 1 local pname = "OptionsFrameContainerBody" .. key .. row.parentRow OptionsSearch_Place(pname, prev) getglobal(pname):Show() prev = pname end if not placed[rkey] then placed[rkey] = 1 local name = "OptionsFrameContainerBody" .. key .. rkey OptionsSearch_Place(name, prev) row:Show() prev = name end end OptionsPage_Refresh(key) end end end
-- Ending a search: every page back on its authored chain, heads away, and the -- selection re-applied — SelectCategory re-shows the one body, retitles, and brings -- Defaults back (the era's no-text arm, l.655-658). function OptionsSearch_Restore() OptionsFrameContainerScroll:SetVerticalScroll(0) for k in pairs(OPTIONS_PAGE_ROWS) do OptionsPage_Layout(k) getglobal("OptionsFrameContainerBodySearchHead" .. k):Hide() end for i = 1, KEYBINDINGS_SEARCH_ROWS do getglobal("OptionsFrameContainerBodyKeybindSearch" .. i):Hide() end getglobal("OptionsFrameContainerBodySearchHeadKeybindings"):Hide() KeyBindingsPage.searchPainted = nil OptionsFrameContainerBodyNoResults:Hide() OptionsFrameContainerDefaults:Show() OptionsFrame_SelectCategory(OptionsFrame.selectedCategory or "Controls") end
-- The text gate (era OnSearchTextChanged l.640-652): a repeat of the same text is a -- no-op, and the FIRST change (searchText still nil — load-time initialization) -- arms without acting; text clearing restores only if a search was actually live. function OptionsSearch_OnTextChanged(text) if text == OptionsFrame.searchText then return end local had = OptionsFrame.searchText and OptionsFrame.searchText ~= "" OptionsFrame.searchText = text if text == "" then if had then OptionsSearch_Restore() end else OptionsSearch_Display(text) end end
-- ── The setting pages: 1.12 rows in the era Settings grammar ──────────────────────── -- One machinery, every page (Audio 0957, the first). Semantics (rows, CVars, labels, -- dependencies, the click-sound quirk) are the 1.12 client's own panels, quoted -- verbatim (SoundOptionsFrame.lua / OptionsFrame.lua + GlobalStrings.lua); geometry is -- the era settings list (Blizzard_SettingControls.xml/.lua + Blizzard_SettingsList.lua -- @1.15.9 — 26-tall rows on a 9 spacing, label LEFT+37 → CENTER-85, control at -- CENTER-80, child rows +15 indent in the small font). Era rows with no 1.12 CVar + -- benilla knob behind them (Enable Sound=Sound_EnableAllSound, Dialog, output device, -- channels…) do not ship — the 0950 honest-tree rule applied to settings. OPTIONS_PAGE_ROWS = { Controls = { "RowStickyTarget", "RowAutoLoot", "RowInvertMouse", "RowMouseSpeed", "RowMaxCameraDistance", }, Audio = { "RowEnableAll", "RowMaster", "RowSound", "RowMusic", "RowAmbience", "RowEnableMusic", "RowEnableAmbience", }, Graphics = { "RowUiScale", "RowWorldDetail" }, Nameplates = { "RowPlayerNames", "RowNpcNames", "RowOwnName" }, -- The stock globals that were already defined AND consumed when 1134 opened the store -- (1136; Buff Durations 1139), in the reference's own on-screen order — its Basic -- Options anchor chain, Display block (CheckButton42 → 39 → 66) before Help (29). Interface = { "RowStatusText", "RowInstantQuestText", "RowBuffDurations", "RowAutoQuestWatch", "RowNewbieTips", }, -- The two chat-bubble switches (decision 1139), in the reference's relative order — -- its Advanced Options chat chain runs CheckButton37 → 46 (Loot Spam, no knob of ours) -- → 38, so ours are adjacent with that gap named rather than silently closed. Social = { "RowChatBubbles", "RowPartyChatBubbles" }, -- 1.12's Advanced Options "Action Bars" group is six rows; five of them are the -- multibar show/hide toggles, which read `func = MultiBarN_IsVisible` — not a store at -- all, and our two bottom multibars are always on (MultiBars.xml). So the honest page -- is the sixth (decision 1136). ActionBars = { "RowLockActionBar" }, -- The floating-combat-text family (decision 1134), in the reference's own on-screen -- order — its AdvancedOptionsCombatText box's anchor chain, master → scroll mode → -- the twelve, NOT its check-button index order (which jumps 58→60→63…59→69). Combat = { "RowCombatText", "RowFloatMode", "RowLowHealthMana", "RowAuras", "RowAuraFade", "RowCombatState", "RowDodgeParryMiss", "RowResistances", "RowReputation", "RowReactives", "RowFriendlyNames", "RowComboPoints", "RowEnergyGains", "RowHonorGained", }, }
-- `tip` is the GlobalStrings KEY of the row's description (B223, decision 1054) — the key, -- not the text: it resolves at HOVER, the way the 1.12 Interface panel resolves its own -- (UIOptionsFrame.lua l.265, `getglobal("OPTION_TOOLTIP_"..key)`), so the row is wired -- before GlobalStrings has to exist. nil = no 1.12 string for this setting (Auto Loot). function OptionsRow_OnLoad(row, cvar, label, tip, child) row.cvar = cvar row.tip = tip -- The search tag: the era's default is exactly the setting's display name -- (SettingControls.lua l.773 AddSearchTags(name)), uppercased at registration -- (Blizzard_Settings.lua l.60). row.searchTag = string.upper(label) -- Kept, not just applied: the disabled-state font (OptionsRow_SetEnabled) has to pick -- the SAME size the indent chose, or greying a child row also promotes it. row.child = child local l = getglobal(row:GetName() .. "Label") l:SetText(label) if child then -- era child rows: +15 label indent and the small font -- (SettingControls.lua l.319-322); the control itself does not indent. l:SetFontObject("GameFontNormalSmall") l:ClearAllPoints() l:SetPoint("LEFT", row:GetName(), "LEFT", 52, 0) l:SetPoint("RIGHT", row:GetName(), "CENTER", -85, 0) end end
-- ── The row's STORE: a CVar, or a saved-variable global (decision 1134) ──────────── -- 1.12's own Interface panel has TWO stores, not one: each UIOptionsFrameCheckButtons -- entry carries either `cvar = "name"` (an engine knob) or `uvar = "GLOBAL"` (a -- RegisterForSave'd Lua global), and UIOptionsFrame_Load/_Save fork on exactly that field -- (UIOptionsFrame.lua l.230-377). Values are strings either way — "1"/"0" for a toggle — -- so only the accessor differs, and every row in this file now reads and writes through -- this trio instead of calling Get/SetCVar directly. function OptionsRow_Get(row) if row.uvar then return getglobal(row.uvar) end return GetCVar(row.cvar) end
-- The write. A global's consumers are Lua and do not poll, so a uvar row also runs its -- `applyFunc` — the reference's own per-uvar side effects (SIMPLE_CHAT → FCF_Set_*, -- HIDE_PARTY_INTERFACE → RaidOptionsFrame_UpdatePartyFrames, the combat-text family → -- CombatText_UpdateDisplayedMessages), moved from its batched Okay to our live write -- because this window commits on the click (0961's grammar), not on a Save button. -- `cvarEvent` is a CVar row's counterpart to a global row's `applyFunc`, and it is the -- reference's own third SetCVar argument (decision 1140): the token the engine hands back -- as `CVAR_UPDATE`'s arg1. 1.12 passes its CheckButtons table KEY there -- (`SetCVar(value.cvar, value.value, index)`), so a consumer that wants to react the -- INSTANT the switch moves — rather than on its next repaint — has something to listen -- for. nil on a row nobody listens to, which is most of them: the host polls its knob. function OptionsRow_Set(row, value) if row.uvar then setglobal(row.uvar, value) if row.applyFunc then row.applyFunc() end return end SetCVar(row.cvar, value, row.cvarEvent) end
-- The registered default — GetCVarDefault's counterpart for a global. `udefault` is the -- value the defining XML assigned at FILE SCOPE, captured at this row's OnLoad: the whole -- UI's XML loads before the saved-variables chunk executes over it (decision 1128's load -- order), so at OnLoad the global still holds its shipped default. That makes the -- assignment the single source of the default — the panel restates nothing and so cannot -- drift from it, where the reference's table carries a second hand-written copy. function OptionsRow_Default(row) if row.uvar then return row.udefault end return GetCVarDefault(row.cvar) end
-- A row whose store is a saved-variable global rather than a CVar. Same signature as -- OptionsRow_OnLoad with the global's name in the cvar seat; the caller adds `applyFunc` -- afterwards when the setting needs one. function OptionsGlobalRow_OnLoad(row, uvar, label, tip, child) OptionsRow_OnLoad(row, nil, label, tip, child) row.uvar = uvar row.udefault = getglobal(uvar) end
-- The other end of `applyFunc`, and the reason a saved "off" used to come back on -- (decision 1139). A CVar row needs nothing here — the host reads its own table at boot. -- A GLOBAL row does: the whole UI's XML runs BEFORE the saved chunk executes over it -- (1128's load order), so every file-scope consumer already ran against the SHIPPED -- default — CombatText_OnLoad armed six event registrations from SHOW_COMBAT_TEXT = "1", -- BuffFrame seated its rows from the durations-shown geometry — and the saved value -- landing afterwards changed the variable while leaving the world it configured alone. -- -- 1.12 closes this with a hand-written ladder in UIOptionsFrame's VARIABLES_LOADED arm -- (l.204-220, "Option specific function calls": BuffButtons_UpdatePositions, the -- SIMPLE_CHAT/CHAT_LOCKED arms, MultiActionBar_ShowAllGrids). We already hold each side -- effect on its own row, so the ladder is a walk: run every distinct applyFunc once, in -- no particular order (they are independent by construction — each one re-derives one -- feature's state from one global). A row whose defining file was not loaded has a nil -- applyFunc and is skipped, which is what keeps a partial test harness honest. function OptionsFrame_ApplySavedSettings() local ran = {} for key, rows in pairs(OPTIONS_PAGE_ROWS) do for _, rkey in ipairs(rows) do local row = getglobal("OptionsFrameContainerBody" .. key .. rkey) local apply = row and row.applyFunc if apply and not ran[apply] then ran[apply] = 1 apply() end end end end
-- A slider row's own range and readout, when the template's 0..1 / 5% / percent (the -- volume shape) isn't it — called after OptionsRow_OnLoad in the row's OnLoad. The -- refreshing guard: SetMinMaxValues re-clamps the held value and fires OnValueChanged, -- and that clamp is wiring, not a player gesture — without the guard every load would -- SetCVar the template's 0 clamped into the new range. function OptionsSliderRow_Setup(row, min, max, step, fmt) local slider = getglobal(row:GetName() .. "ControlSlider") row.fmt = fmt row.refreshing = 1 slider:SetMinMaxValues(min, max) slider:SetValueStep(step) row.refreshing = nil end
-- ── The dropdown rows (0992): the 1.12 kit under the era row grammar ──────────────── -- A dropdown row's choices: entries = { {text=..., value=...}, ... }, values the CVar's -- own strings. The kit does the rest: every open re-runs the init through the stored -- initialize (Toggle's own law), and AddButton auto-checks the entry matching the -- capsule's selectedValue — which OptionsDropdown_ShowValue keeps equal to the CVar. function OptionsDropdownRow_Setup(row, entries) row.entries = entries local dd = getglobal(row:GetName() .. "Dropdown") UIDropDownMenu_SetWidth(180, dd) UIDropDownMenu_Initialize(dd, OptionsDropdownRow_InitMenu) -- The capsule's toggle button is a mouse-enabled child — it steals hover from the -- row, so it carries the row wash like the checkbox rows' box does. Hooked here -- (SetScript) because the capsule template is the shared kit's, not this file's. local btn = getglobal(dd:GetName() .. "Button") btn:SetScript("OnEnter", function() OptionsRow_Hover(this:GetParent():GetParent(), 1) end) btn:SetScript("OnLeave", function() OptionsRow_Hover(this:GetParent():GetParent(), nil) end) end
function OptionsDropdownRow_InitMenu() local dd = getglobal(UIDROPDOWNMENU_INIT_MENU) local row = dd:GetParent() for _, e in ipairs(row.entries) do local info = {} info.text = e.text info.value = e.value info.func = OptionsDropdownEntry_OnClick UIDropDownMenu_AddButton(info) end end
-- The entry click (`this` = the list row, the kit's own calling law): the write, then -- the capsule redisplay. The kit closes the list and plays its own click sound. function OptionsDropdownEntry_OnClick() local dd = UIDropDownMenu_GetCurrentDropDown() local row = dd:GetParent() OptionsRow_Set(row, this.value) OptionsDropdown_ShowValue(row) end
-- Paint the capsule from the CVar. selectedValue is written as a FIELD, not through -- SetSelectedValue: that helper's Refresh walks the SHARED DropDownList1 buttons, which -- may still hold another dropdown's rows on this refresh path (the list is closed) — -- a foreign row matching by value would repaint our capsule with its text. An off-grid -- CVar value (an env A/B, a hand edit) displays the NEAREST stop — 0959's out-of-range -- law, dropdown-flavored: control and check agree on the nearest expressible value, -- the engine keeps running the config's truth, nothing writes back until the player -- actually picks an entry. (A non-numeric stray shows raw and checks nothing.) function OptionsDropdown_ShowValue(row) local dd = getglobal(row:GetName() .. "Dropdown") local v = OptionsRow_Get(row) local match for _, e in ipairs(row.entries) do if e.value == v then match = e end end if not match and tonumber(v) then local best for _, e in ipairs(row.entries) do local d = tonumber(e.value) and math.abs(tonumber(e.value) - tonumber(v)) if d and (not best or d < best) then best = d match = e end end end if match then dd.selectedValue = match.value UIDropDownMenu_SetText(match.text, dd) else dd.selectedValue = v UIDropDownMenu_SetText(v, dd) end end
-- The right-hand readout text (era MinimalSlider's RIGHT label seat): rounded percent -- (era FormatPercentage, Audio.lua l.406-411) unless the row asked for the raw number. function OptionsRow_FormatValue(row, value) if row.fmt == "raw" then return string.format("%d", math.floor(value + 0.5)) end -- A row whose stored value is a FACTOR but whose meaning is a distance: show the -- distance (decision 1140 — cameraDistanceMaxFactor over the 15 yd base). The number -- the player is choosing is "how far out the wheel stops", not "times 1.4". if row.fmt == "yards" then return string.format("%d yd", math.floor(value * 15 + 0.5)) end return string.format("%d%%", math.floor(value * 100 + 0.5)) end
-- The era row-wide hover wash (HoverBackgroundTemplate, white a=0.1): the row and every -- control on it show the SAME texture, so crossing from label to slider doesn't blink. -- ONE seam carries the wash AND the plate (B223): every surface that lights the row also -- raises its tooltip, so the two can never disagree — and the crossing is still seamless, -- since the engine fires OnLeave before OnEnter within a move (pointer.rs), leaving the -- hide/re-show inside a single frame. function OptionsRow_Hover(row, on) local hover = getglobal(row:GetName() .. "Hover") if on then hover:Show() OptionsRow_ShowTooltip(row) else hover:Hide() GameTooltip:Hide() end end
-- The row's descriptive plate (B223, decision 1054). -- STRING: 1.12's own per-option text, by GlobalStrings key (see OptionsRow_OnLoad). A row -- with no 1.12 string raises NOTHING — a plate whose only line echoes the label the cursor -- is on is noise, and inventing a description would be inventing fidelity. -- SHAPE: the 1.12/1.14 option-row plate — the description alone, wrapped, in the tooltip's -- default gold (OptionsFrameTemplates.xml l.52-64: SetOwner + SetText(text, …, 1)); this -- window already wears it on the Keybindings page's Character Specific row (1008). The era -- pair (a white name line over the description) is cut — see the SCOPE note. -- SEAT: the era's (DefaultTooltipMixin.OnEnter — ANCHOR_RIGHT, x -10, off the row's LABEL -- half), carried by the $parentTip region, so the plate opens at the same column on every -- row whichever surface the cursor crossed. function OptionsRow_ShowTooltip(row) local text = row.tip and getglobal(row.tip) if text then GameTooltip:SetOwner(getglobal(row:GetName() .. "Tip"), "ANCHOR_RIGHT", -10, 0) GameTooltip:SetText(text, nil, nil, nil, nil, 1) else -- A mute row PUTS AWAY whatever the last row raised. Entering a row asserts "this -- row's plate is what shows", so an early return isn't enough: the ordinary cursor -- path is saved by the outgoing row's own OnLeave, but any caller that enters -- without one (a driven hover, a re-layout under the cursor) would leave the -- neighbour's description standing over a row it doesn't describe — a plate saying -- the wrong thing is worse than a row saying nothing. 1.12's own handler has the -- bare early-out; this is deliberate, and it is why the mute case has a test. GameTooltip:Hide() end end
function OptionsCheckbox_OnClick(box) local row = box:GetParent() local checked = box:GetChecked() -- Click kits: the 1.12 panels disagree with EACH OTHER — the interface panel's -- PlayClickSound maps checked→CheckBoxOn (OptionsFrame.lua l.509), while the sound -- panel's own OnClick maps checked→CheckBoxOff (SoundOptionsFrame.lua, the 0957 -- quirk) — so each page keeps its own panel's mapping (soundQuirk on Audio rows). local kitOn = checked if row.soundQuirk then kitOn = not kitOn end if kitOn then PlaySound("igMainMenuOptionCheckBoxOn") else PlaySound("igMainMenuOptionCheckBoxOff") end -- The write: checked = 1 — unless the row is value-INVERTED (Sticky Targeting: -- 1.12 checks it when deselectOnClick is "0", era wraps the same CVar in -- NegateBoolean; both references agree). local on = checked if row.invert then on = not on end if on then OptionsRow_Set(row, "1") else OptionsRow_Set(row, "0") end OptionsPage_UpdateDependencies(OptionsFrame.selectedCategory) end
function OptionsSlider_OnValueChanged(slider, value) local control = slider:GetParent() local row = control:GetParent() if not row.refreshing then -- era obeyStepOnDrag (MinimalSlider.xml l.5-7): user moves snap to the step -- grid — anchored at the range MINIMUM, the reference slider's own anchor -- (farclip's 1.12 grid is 177+n*60, not the multiples of 60). A refresh -- writes the stored value raw (era SetValue does not snap), so an off-grid -- config value still lands where it said. local step = slider:GetValueStep() if step and step > 0 then local minv = slider:GetMinMaxValues() local snapped = minv + math.floor((value - minv) / step + 0.5) * step if math.abs(snapped - value) > 0.00001 then slider:SetValue(snapped) -- re-enters once with the snapped value return end value = snapped -- the clean grid number, not the f32-rounded echo end end getglobal(control:GetName() .. "Value"):SetText(OptionsRow_FormatValue(row, value)) if (row.cvar or row.uvar) and not row.refreshing then -- Two decimals cover every page's grid (the 5% volumes, uiScale's 0.01, whole -- yards); trailing zeros stripped so a value at the registered default -- compares equal to it as a STRING and stays out of the config file ("0.40" -- would read as moved-off-"0.4"). local str = string.gsub(string.format("%.2f", value), "%.?0+$", "") if row.deferred then -- era CommitFlag.Apply, transcribed (Blizzard_Setting.lua's staged -- SetValue half): the control shows the new value, the ENGINE keeps the -- old one, and the CVar moves only when Apply commits — dragging a -- slider that rescales itself mid-drag is exactly what this flag -- exists to prevent. Dragging back onto the committed value clears the -- pending (era's IsModified: a pending EQUAL to current isn't one). if str == OptionsRow_Get(row) then row.pending = nil else row.pending = str end OptionsApply_Update() else OptionsRow_Set(row, str) end end end
function OptionsPage_Refresh(key) local base = "OptionsFrameContainerBody" .. key for _, rkey in ipairs(OPTIONS_PAGE_ROWS[key]) do local row = getglobal(base .. rkey) local box = getglobal(base .. rkey .. "Check") if box then -- SetChecked takes the CVar string exactly like the 1.12 panel: the numeric -- read means "0" unchecks (button-check-and-state-texture.md). A -- value-inverted row checks on "0" instead — UIOptionsFrame.lua's own -- GAMEFIELD_DESELECT arm (`checked = 1` when the CVar reads "0"). if row.invert then local checked if OptionsRow_Get(row) == "0" then checked = 1 end box:SetChecked(checked) else box:SetChecked(OptionsRow_Get(row)) end elseif row.entries then OptionsDropdown_ShowValue(row) else local slider = getglobal(base .. rkey .. "ControlSlider") row.refreshing = 1 -- Pending first (era GetValue returns the pendingValue while one is -- staged): coming back to a page with an un-applied edit shows the edit. slider:SetValue(tonumber(row.pending or OptionsRow_Get(row) or "0") or 0) row.refreshing = nil -- SetValue fires only on a CHANGE — write the readout unconditionally, -- from the slider's OWN value: in range that IS the CVar (SetValue stores -- raw), out of range the thumb and the number at least agree on the -- nearest expressible value. getglobal(base .. rkey .. "ControlValue"):SetText( OptionsRow_FormatValue(row, slider:GetValue())) end end OptionsPage_UpdateDependencies(key) OptionsApply_Update() end
-- Per-page dependency rules. Audio's is the 1.12 rule, verbatim: Enable All Sound off -- greys Enable Ambience — and only it, of our rows -- (SoundOptionsFrame_UpdateDependencies disables buttons 2 and 4, Ambience and Error -- Speech; Enable Music stays live, the panel's own quirk). function OptionsPage_UpdateDependencies(key) if key == "Combat" then -- The 1.12 rule, verbatim (UIOptionsFrame_UpdateDependencies' "Additional combat -- text dependancies" block): the master off greys EVERY sub-toggle and the scroll -- dropdown. Combo Points carries the reference's second gate too — it is disabled -- for anyone who is not a rogue or a druid, since nobody else has combo points. local on = SHOW_COMBAT_TEXT ~= "0" local _, class = UnitClass("player") class = class and string.upper(class) local combo = class == "ROGUE" or class == "DRUID" for _, rkey in ipairs(OPTIONS_PAGE_ROWS.Combat) do if rkey ~= "RowCombatText" then local live = on if rkey == "RowComboPoints" and not combo then live = nil end OptionsRow_SetEnabled( getglobal("OptionsFrameContainerBodyCombat" .. rkey), live) end end return end if key ~= "Audio" then return end local on = GetCVar("MasterSoundEffects") ~= "0" local box = OptionsFrameContainerBodyAudioRowEnableAmbienceCheck local label = OptionsFrameContainerBodyAudioRowEnableAmbienceLabel if on then box:Enable() label:SetFontObject("GameFontNormal") else box:Disable() label:SetFontObject("GameFontDisable") end end
-- Grey or wake one row, whichever control it wears (the Audio rule above predates this and -- reaches its one checkbox by name). A dropdown row greys the way 1.12's own -- OptionsFrame_DisableDropDown does — the capsule's toggle BUTTON disabled so the list -- cannot open, and its text in GRAY_FONT_COLOR — since our kit's -- UIDropDownMenu_DisableButton addresses a LIST row (level, id), not the capsule. function OptionsRow_SetEnabled(row, on) local name = row:GetName() local box = getglobal(name .. "Check") local dd = getglobal(name .. "Dropdown") if box then if on then box:Enable() else box:Disable() end elseif dd then local text = getglobal(dd:GetName() .. "Text") if on then getglobal(dd:GetName() .. "Button"):Enable() text:SetTextColor(HIGHLIGHT_FONT_COLOR.r, HIGHLIGHT_FONT_COLOR.g, HIGHLIGHT_FONT_COLOR.b) else getglobal(dd:GetName() .. "Button"):Disable() text:SetTextColor(GRAY_FONT_COLOR.r, GRAY_FONT_COLOR.g, GRAY_FONT_COLOR.b) end end local label = getglobal(name .. "Label") if on then label:SetFontObject(row.child and "GameFontNormalSmall" or "GameFontNormal") else label:SetFontObject(row.child and "GameFontDisableSmall" or "GameFontDisable") end end
-- Defaults, live on any page with rows: every row's CVar back to its registered -- default (era resets per-setting the same way; the era all-pages confirm dialog is -- not modeled — Defaults resets the VISIBLE page). A pending edit dies with it — the -- default write supersedes what Apply would have committed. function OptionsPage_Defaults(key) local base = "OptionsFrameContainerBody" .. key for _, rkey in ipairs(OPTIONS_PAGE_ROWS[key]) do local row = getglobal(base .. rkey) row.pending = nil OptionsRow_Set(row, OptionsRow_Default(row)) end OptionsPage_Refresh(key) end
-- ── The Apply flow (0961): era CommitFlag.Apply, cut to our rows ──────────────────── -- Pending edits are PANEL-wide like era's modified table: they survive a category -- switch (the row redisplays its pending on return) and commit together; only hiding -- the window discards them (era wipes on hide too — its close-time 3-button confirm -- dialog and the 8-second revert timer are not modeled, SCOPE note).
-- The era Apply gate (HasUnappliedSettings + SetApplyButtonEnabled): the button is -- enabled AND shown together — it EXISTS only while something is pending. function OptionsApply_Update() local pending for key, rows in pairs(OPTIONS_PAGE_ROWS) do local base = "OptionsFrameContainerBody" .. key for _, rkey in ipairs(rows) do if getglobal(base .. rkey).pending then pending = 1 end end end if pending then OptionsFrameApplyButton:Enable() OptionsFrameApplyButton:Show() else OptionsFrameApplyButton:Disable() OptionsFrameApplyButton:Hide() end end
-- Commit (era SettingsPanelMixin:CommitSettings, cut to our rows): every pending -- value everywhere becomes a real SetCVar, and the button goes away. function OptionsPage_Apply() for key, rows in pairs(OPTIONS_PAGE_ROWS) do local base = "OptionsFrameContainerBody" .. key for _, rkey in ipairs(rows) do local row = getglobal(base .. rkey) if row.pending then OptionsRow_Set(row, row.pending) row.pending = nil end end end OptionsApply_Update() end
-- Hide = discard (era's WipeModifiedTable-on-hide; the confirm dialog is cut): the -- next open re-reads the committed CVars, so the sliders land back on the truth. function OptionsPage_DiscardPending() for key, rows in pairs(OPTIONS_PAGE_ROWS) do local base = "OptionsFrameContainerBody" .. key for _, rkey in ipairs(rows) do getglobal(base .. rkey).pending = nil end end OptionsApply_Update() end
